steps.do: Create the prompt that turns any inbound support message into one strict JSON record. A prompt in CALIBER is a reusable, versioned instruction template. Choose the Write / paste on-ramp and paste the template body.
fill: the body of intake-classifier.md (everything below the YAML front matter)
steps.see: The workspace opens on Author; the version history lists v1 with a live badge.

steps.do: Introduce the regression as a draft: replace the template with the weaker wording that drops the JSON-only rules. A draft registers a version without touching the live alias, because authoring is not deploying.
steps.see: v2 appears in the version history; v1 keeps the live badge.

steps.do: Import the labelled test set from the file. The Calibration stage's Upload JSON/JSONL reads one example per line (input and expected keys) and creates the test set. The set has 44 realistic cases: billing, account access, how-to, bugs, cancellations, security, prompt injection, ambiguous, multilingual, empty and very long messages.
steps.see: Uploaded 44 examples to cookbook-01-intake-golden. and the set is selected under Existing Dataset.

steps.do: Check the imported test set: search for it, then open it to read its rows.
steps.see: The list shows the set at v45; opened, it lists the examples, including I was charged twice after upgrading to the Team plan this morning. and the Ignore all previous instructions... injection.

steps.do: Score the prompt version on the test set. On the alpha's default simulated model this is refused with a clear message, because CALIBER never invents a scorecard. With a model that answers (a real model such as a local Ollama qwen2.5:7b, or the README's stand-in model) it runs: the page waits while every one of the 44 examples is answered (about 45 seconds on a local 7B model).
fill: turn off Exact match and Contains expected; leave Token F1
steps.see: Simulated stack: the red message evaluation requires a real LLM provider; set CALIBER_LLM_PROVIDER .... Stand-in or real model: a completed run with an n/44 examples-passed count (stand-in 34/44; a 7B model about 9/44). If the model is unreachable: a failed run whose page says This run failed: ... with the server's error.

steps.do: (Needs a model that answers.) Run the same evaluation for cookbook-01-intake-classifier@2 with the label weaker v2, open it, and choose the baseline under Compare to. Nothing changed but the prompt text, so the difference is the regression.
steps.see: The comparison context box and pp deltas on Overall and Token F1. With the stand-in: red deltas, the pass rate falling to 0%, and every prediction starting Happy to help! with a Fail result, where the baseline's predictions are bare JSON records. With a real 7B model v2 still answers in JSON; the drop is smaller (token F1 about 0.43 → 0.35).
steps.asset: regression evidence: v2 vs v1 baseline

steps.do: Calibrate the live prompt against the test set. Under Scoring untick Correctness, Relevance and Safety and tick Guidelines with the config from guidelines.json (Correctness needs an expected response this test set does not have). On the simulated stack, first set a gate no simulated candidate can pass, to see a gate block, then set it back. On a real model keep the defaults on a hosted model, or lower the gate for a noisy local 7B model.
fill: untick Correctness, Relevance, Safety; tick Guidelines and paste the config
0.99 (first run, blocked, simulated stack only), then 0.85 (local 7B model: 0.3, with Maximum regression delta 0.25)
steps.see: Simulated stack: the 0.99 run ends rejected with no Review & apply; the 0.85 run reaches a candidate within seconds. Real model: a candidate after about 5 to 8 minutes on a local 7B model (or a rejected run with the reason, if the judge scores it under the gate).

steps.do: Review the candidate before anything changes: the prompt diff, the evidence, the gate. On the simulated stack the evidence is canned and says so. Applying is the explicit, separate decision.
steps.see: Review candidate before applying shows the diff (+3 / -0 lines), Simulated evaluation — not evidence (simulated stack; on a real model no banner and measured Baseline, Candidate and Change scores), 44 evaluation examples and Gate: Passed. After Apply: Candidate applied. and on Author the live badge is on v3.

steps.do: Verify the release on the live board and the timeline. Both name who applied it.
steps.see: What's live now has the prompt at v3 @prod by admin; the Timeline shows Promote ... v1 → v3 ... admin.
steps.asset: live board and timeline show v3

steps.do: Verify the audit trail: filter by the prompt's name.
steps.see: promote_prompt rows by admin; the newest carries "eval_simulated":"true" in its details ("false" on a real model).

steps.do: Roll back. In the version history, roll back the live version and confirm.
steps.see: The live badge returns to v1. On Releases the live row says v1 and the timeline's newest entry is Roll back ... v3 → v1 ... admin; the audit log has rollback_prompt by admin.
